title: an-unbuildable-network-seal-refuses-the-run
intention: A proof whose network seal the tester cannot build is refused before it runs and nothing is persisted, so an unbuildable seal never lands in a record of truth as a RED verdict about the proof.
why: Measured 2026-10-06 under 72a37498c601: proofgate rewrote a crossing that named a proof as an argument into bin/cairn test --exec, and the cairn test --seal beside it ran nested. Inside --exec the instance seal inherits (c54d744aa9ac) but the network seal cannot: NetnsIsolation.available() says False (isolation.py:753-762), run_proof mints Seal('indeterminate') and runs the subject anyway (device.py:522-524), wrap() still emits bwrap --unshare-net, the subject dies 'bwrap: No permissions to create a new namespace', and --seal persists that as the proof's RED (device.py:759-779). The record then says the proof failed when what failed was the harness — a false verdict in a record of truth (Law 7), and a red a peer leans on (Law 8). Inheriting is ruled out by measurement: inside --exec the route is open (connect to 1.1.1.1:443 succeeded, default route present, CAIRN_TESTER_SEALED unset, CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED=1). 68cef2ddd8ef routes verdict instruments through --exec, and any instrument that is itself cairn test --seal would land this false red.
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are permanent in records of truth, and a record of truth may not carry a false verdict: the harness failed, not the proof) and Law 8 (a false red persisted as a validation is a record a peer leans on); RULE 1 (the fix lives inside the tester, measured only there)
how: In TesterDevice.run_proof, where iso.seals_network and not iso.available() today mints Seal('indeterminate') and runs the subject anyway (wrap() still emits bwrap --unshare-net, which dies 'No permissions to create a new namespace'), raise a refusal (SealUnavailable, a ValueError beside SealDowngradeRefused) before anything runs or persists. cairn test catches it into its existing REFUSED lane (exit nonzero, nothing persisted, reason printed); the hollow turns it into HollowUnmeasurable (exit 2); the reseal door reports it as a refusal and seals nothing. Inheriting the outer seal is ruled out by measurement: inside bin/cairn test --exec the network is OPEN (2026-10-06, n=1: connect to 1.1.1.1:443 succeeded, default route present, CAIRN_TESTER_SEALED unset, CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED=1), so an inherited net seal would record sealed over an open route. The proof berths at cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_an_unbuildable_network_seal_refuses_the_run.py: it builds a green fixture proof in a tmp dir and drives run_proof / bin/cairn test / --hollow in a subprocess whose env carries CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED=1 and lacks CAIRN_TESTER_SEALED, so no real nested namespace is needed and the live validation store is never written.
falsifier: RED if after the build: (1) run_proof(proof, sink='validations', isolation='netns') with CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED=1 and CAIRN_TESTER_SEALED unset in its environment runs the subject or writes a validation, instead of raising the refusal; (2) bin/cairn test --seal over that proof under the same markers exits 0, or prints no REFUSED line, or the proof's validation file changes; (3) bin/cairn test --hollow under the same markers measures a proof at netns instead of exiting 2. WRONG INTENT if the outer --exec wrap is measured to cut the network (then the seal should inherit, not refuse). Horizon: the tester seal of the new proof.
watchme: none, because the proof the build writes beside cairn/devices/tester/device.py reds on drift, and every refusal prints a REFUSED line at the cairn test surface (cairn/devices/tester/cli.py)
children: none, because one raise in cairn/devices/tester/device.py, one except arm each in cli.py and hollow.py, and one proof
questions: none, because the peer akiendelllinux_cc_0 set the rule on 2026-10-06 (inherit only if measured sealed, else refuse and persist nothing) and the measurement chose refuse; the branch is in cairn/devices/tester/device.py, beside ticket c54d744aa9ac
